title: SLO adoption experiments and ops surface map
content:
Purpose

This doc is a lightweight, experimental surface map for running a concise, hypothesis-driven SLO adoption program across product, platform, and SRE teams. The goal: create rapid small-batch experiments that produce observable operational improvement (reduced P99 latency spikes, fewer deploy-induced errors, clearer escalation paths), then convert successful experiments into repeatable runbooks and rollout templates.

Why this is different

- Focus on small, measurable experiments (2–6 week cycles) rather than a single large SLO rollout.
- Emphasis on cross-team minimal viable guardrails (not perfect SLO design up-front).
- Surface map approach: document where signals live, who touches them, and friction points for handoff.

Scope (what we will cover)

- Target services: inference-proxy, request-router, tokenizer, batch-cache (first wave)
- Signals: latency histograms, error rates (4xx/5xx split), queue depth, autoscaler actions, request drop counts, rollout metrics (canary fail rate)
- Owners: product feature owner + oncall SRE + platform engineer for each experiment

High-level success criteria (for experiment to be promoted)

- Clear, repeatable measurement that shows >=15% reduction in rolling P99 latency spikes or 25% reduction in 5xx incidence during normal traffic for the target service within the experiment window.
- Team can run a tabletop and demonstrate escalation path in <20 minutes.
- Implementation requires <2 engineer-weeks for the owning team (SRE + product).

Experiment cadence and structure

- Duration: 2–6 weeks, recommended 3 weeks.
- Week 0: kick (setup metrics, dashboards, baseline), define hypothesis & owner, document rollback & safety boundaries.
- Week 1: implement smallest change (tweak batching config, enable prefix KV cache for a subset of routes, tune autoscaler threshold), run smoke tests.
- Week 2: run in production with feature flag/canary, collect signals daily.
- Week 3: retro and decision — promote to runbook, iterate, or abandon.

Example experiments (starting points)

1) Prefix cache warm-up trial (inference-proxy)
   - Hypothesis: Pre-warming top-10 prefixes for high-volume routes reduces P50/P95/P99 by shifting cache hit distribution.
   - Action: Add background warm-up for top routes for 48h behind a feature flag.
   - Measurements: cache hit ratio, P95/P99 latency, cost delta (compute cycles).
   - Safeguards: automatic rollback if error rate increases by >5% absolute.

2) Autoscaler hysteresis tuning (request-router)
   - Hypothesis: Slightly longer scale-down cooldown reduces scale-churn and transient latency spikes during modest traffic bursts.
   - Action: adjust scale-down window from 30s->90s in dedicated pool (canary on low-traffic region).
   - Measurements: # of scale events/hour, P99 during burst tests.

3) Client-side batching toggle (batch-cache)
   - Hypothesis: Enforcing a minimum batching window for low-rate tenants reduces per-token cost and evens service tail latency.
   - Action: opt-in tenant sample for 2 weeks.
   - Measurements: per-tenant cost, tail latency, user-perceived latency.

Surface map: signals, owners, friction points

- Metric stores: Prometheus (latency histograms), DataDog (synthetic checks), BigQuery (rollup logs)
  Owners: Observability infra (Julien)
  Friction: duplicate metric names, cardinality explosion; need canonical metric mapping doc.

- Alerts & Pager rules: PagerDuty -> SRE oncall rota
  Owners: SRE ops lead (Priya)
  Friction: Alert noise during experiments. Solution: temporary suppressions with clear expiry and burn-down plan.

- Dashboards: per-service experiment dashboards (latency, errors, cache hit, scaling)
  Owners: Product / SRE collaborative pair
  Friction: dashboard divergence; enforce a template and single source-of-truth graph ids.

Onboarding checklist for a service to join program

- Confirm service owner and oncall SRE.
- Create experiment ticket (Jira key) with hypothesis, rollback criteria, timeframe.
- Register experiment in central tracker (linked_artifacts) and create a Slack experiment channel.
- Baseline metrics snapshot (export P50/P95/P99 and error rates for last 7 days).
- Prepare a one-slide runbook with what to revert and who to call.

Communication plan

- Kick: 15m async announcement + 30m kickoff call with all stakeholders.
- Daily check-in: 10–15m async updates in experiment Slack channel (pinned dashboard snapshots).
- Weekly sync: 30m demo + decision for next action.
- Retro: 60m with SRE, product, infra; produce short retro notes and chosen outcome.

Decision rubric

- Promote to runbook: experiment meets success metrics and cost delta acceptable (<10% cost increase or clearly justified).
- Iterate: partial wins or tooling gaps; schedule follow-up 3-week experiment.
- Abandon: no measurable impact or negative side effects. Document learning.

Runbook template (minimal)

- Title, service, experiment id (Jira), date promoted.
- Trigger conditions (exact metric thresholds) and monitoring links.
- Step-by-step mitigation and rollback steps (with exact CLI/console commands).
- Communication steps (who pages, channels, escalation).

Risk register (quick skim)

- Risk: Alert fatigue during experiment. Mitigation: temporary suppression and targeted filters.
- Risk: Hidden cost increase. Mitigation: include cost monitoring in baseline + daily check.
- Risk: Cross-region behavioral differences. Mitigation: run canary in low traffic region first.

Open questions / TODOs

- Can we add an experiment flagging utility to auto-create the experiment channel + dashboard template? (tech spike)
- Need canonical metric dictionary mapping Prometheus -> DataDog -> BigQuery. Assign: Julien
- Explore automated rollback hook in feature flag system when error delta >X. Assign: Platform team

Appendix: quick links and templates

- Experiment ticket template (paste into Jira): 
  - Summary: [service] — [short hypothesis] — [experiment id]
  - Acceptance criteria: metrics & thresholds
  - Rollback plan: commands + contacts
  - Duration: 2–6 weeks

- Slack channel naming convention: #exp-slo-<service>-<id>
- Dashboard template ids: (refer to central dashboard library)

Notes to self (scratchpad)

- Keep experiments cheap and reversible.
- Encourage broad participation by making the onboarding path <1 hour of setup.
- Capture everything in short, searchable artifacts (one-slide promoted runbook).

If you want, I can convert this into a short checklist sheet and pre-populate one experiment ticket for inference-proxy as a working example.
